title: Calibration (sensor model)
description: A calibration is a first-class, versioned, content-addressed artifact -- not metadata attached to a dataset. Entries are TIME-INDEXED even when there is only one, because a fixed calibration is the degenerate case of a drifting one, and code written against the general shape needs no change the day someone hands you a before/after bracket. This schema fixes the SHAPE of a valid calibration; the physics lives in the analysis hub, which is free to argue about it.

calibration_id.description: Content-addressed. A calibration change produces a NEW id; it never mutates an existing artifact. That is what makes it possible to swap one id and re-derive every affected trace, and to know exactly which downstream fits went stale.

kind.description: What sort of sensor model this is. IR background subtraction and reference-spectrum selection are transformations with their own artifacts, not silent preprocessing -- so they are calibrations here, not hidden steps in a script.

entries.description: Time-indexed entries, expected in ascending valid_from order. A single entry is legal and is the common case at project start.

valid_until.description: Optional. Absent means 'until the next entry, or indefinitely'.

channels.description: Per-channel calibration coefficients, keyed by the same channel names the dataset uses.

sensitivity.description: Multiplicative factor mapping raw signal to the target quantity.

sensitivity_sigma.description: Uncertainty on the sensitivity. Calibration uncertainty propagates but belongs to neither data nor parameter uncertainty; it is its own artifact, cited in the chain.

units.description: Units of the sensitivity factor itself, written as target-over-source so the conversion is checkable by inspection.

valid_range.description: Optional source-signal range over which this factor was determined. Extrapolating outside it is a judgement call that should be visible.

pressure_normalization.description: Correct this channel for drift in the analyser's own pressure before applying the sensitivity. A quadrupole's count rate tracks chamber pressure, so a sensitivity determined at one pressure misreads at another; the correction is referenced to the pressure at which the factor was determined.

reference_pressure_sigma.description: DRAFT (2026-08): axial-reworked branch. Type B standard uncertainty (JCGM 100:2008) on reference_pressure. Optional; absent means no uncertainty is stated in any record, which routes this stage to the prior-free envelope rather than to a fabricated sigma.

pressure_channel.description: Name of the dataset channel carrying the measured analyser pressure.

form.description: linear_scale: x * (1 + (p_ref - p)/p_ref), the first-order form legacy spreadsheets use. ratio: x * p_ref/p, exact proportionality. They agree to first order and diverge as p departs from p_ref, so which one was applied is not a detail.

baseline.description: A baseline subtracted from this channel that depends on ANOTHER channel, plus a constant. Distinct from a cracking split: a split apportions a known fragmentation of one species onto another mass, whereas this absorbs whatever empirical, signal-tracking background a lab has fitted -- reagent impurity, detector artefact, flow-correlated offset. Keeping the two apart matters because a split is a property of the molecule and transfers between instruments, while a baseline is a property of this rig on this day and does not.

source_channel.description: Channel whose signal drives the slope term. Omit for a constant-only baseline.

slope.description: Subtracted amount per unit of source_channel.

slope_sigma.description: DRAFT (2026-08): axial-reworked branch. Type B standard uncertainty on slope. Optional; absent means none is stated -- envelope, not invention.

intercept_sigma.description: DRAFT (2026-08): axial-reworked branch. Type B standard uncertainty on intercept. Optional; absent means none is stated.

floor.description: Value below which the corrected signal is clamped. Declaring it here is what lets a dataset carry a matching `censoring` block instead of presenting clamped points as measurements. A calibration that clamps and does not say so is the failure this field exists to make impossible.

matrix.description: For kind = ms_fragmentation: the cracking pattern itself. Keys are "<contributing species>-><affected channel>", values the fraction of the contributor's signal appearing on that channel -- so "CO2->CO": 0.0883 means 8.83% of the CO2 signal lands on m/z 28. A partial pattern is legal and normal: labs measure the splits that matter to them, and a full matrix is the same shape grown. This is the artifact that fragmentation_matrix_ref points AT.

matrix_sigma.description: DRAFT (2026-08): axial-reworked branch. Type B standard uncertainties on the cracking pattern, keyed exactly like `matrix` (the same parallel-map shape `declared_unused` uses). Partial is legal: state the sigmas you have, leave the rest to the prior-free envelope.

priors.description: DRAFT (2026-08): axial-reworked branch. Record-sourced priors on individual coefficients, keyed by dotted path within this entry ("matrix.CO->O", "channels.CO.sensitivity"). Exists for the case where the record itself carries DISAGREEING values -- a declared coefficient, an applied one, and an independent literature value -- and the honest prior is built from that documented spread rather than invented. PEtab's priorDistribution/priorParameters vocabulary, reshaped to this schema's time-indexed entries.

sigma.description: Standard uncertainty, in the coefficient's own units (or decades if the coefficient is stored log-scaled -- say which in source).

source.description: Where this prior comes from, specific enough to re-derive -- e.g. 'spread of declared 0.005905 vs applied 0.0106 vs NIST ~0.017'.

from_declared_unused.description: True when the prior was constructed from the declared/applied discrepancy that `declared_unused` preserves.

declared_unused.description: Coefficients an upstream export DECLARED but did not apply, keyed like `matrix`. Legacy spreadsheets accumulate these: a parameter cell is edited, the formula that once referenced it is replaced by a hard-coded literal, and the two drift apart with nothing to flag it. `matrix` must always carry what was actually applied -- that is what a re-derivation has to reproduce. This field exists so the declared value survives the discrepancy instead of being silently dropped, because which of the two is physically right is a question for the instrument's owner, not for whoever noticed.

reason.description: How the discrepancy was established -- specific enough to re-check, e.g. which cell declared it and how many rows used something else.

fragmentation_matrix_ref.description: For MS: the cracking-pattern matrix, itself a separate cited artifact rather than an inline table, because it is revised independently of the sensitivity factors.

background_ref.description: For IR/XAS: the background or single-beam reference used. A cited artifact, not a silent preprocessing step.

reference_spectrum_ref.description: For XAS: the reference standard used for energy alignment or linear-combination fitting.

determined_from.description: The calibration-gas or standard datasets this entry was fit from. Makes the calibration itself auditable.

owner.description: Who owns the instrument. A calibration change is reviewed by this person -- everything downstream depends on calibration code, so it carries a tighter gate than a fitting tool.

supersedes.description: The calibration this one replaces, if any. Forms an explicit chain instead of leaving readers to sort by date.

notes.description: How this calibration was determined and what its known limits are. The place to record that a fragmentation correction is missing, or that a factor was extrapolated outside its measured range.
